model_annotations.English: This bar chart, titled “RL training data statistic” from the paper “SRPO Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware Reinforcement Learning,” illustrates the number of samples used in the reinforcement learning training dataset, categorized by six distinct types of content. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 14,000, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 2,000. The horizontal axis lists the six categories in the following order: “Other Math,” “Geometric Math,” “Charts Diagrams,” “Natural Science,” and “General Reasoning.” Each category is represented by a single, solid orange bar whose height corresponds to the sample count, with the exact number displayed as a label above each bar. The “Other Math” category has the highest value at 14,333 samples, followed by “Geometric Math” at 10,227, “Charts Diagrams” at 5,953, “General Reasoning” at 3,534, and “Natural Science” at 3,343. The bars are arranged in descending order of sample count from left to right, with no visual emphasis such as shading or bolding applied to any specific bar.

Jeder Balken ist orangefarben und trägt oben die genaue Anzahl der Samples: Der Balken für „Other Math“ erreicht 14.333, der für „Geometric Math“ 10.227, der für „Charts Diagrams“ 5.953, der für „Natural Science“ 3.343 und der für „General Reasoning“ 3.534.
